parties: Quest Capital Markets Limited; CESC Limited
headline: Quest Capital Markets files Regulation 31(4) disclosure under SEBI Takeover Regulations for CESC Limited
sum: Quest Capital Markets Limited has filed a substantial acquisition disclosure (Regulation 31(4)) with the NSE, signalling a material shareholding event in CESC Limited, a major Mumbai-based power utility. The disclosure suggests a mandatory offer trigger under the SEBI Takeover Code and requires public announcement of acquisition intent.
implication: A Regulation 31(4) filing indicates the acquirer has crossed the 25% threshold or intends a control change; the open offer threshold and exemption pathways under Regulation 37 (e.g. creeping acquisition, preferential allotment carve-outs) will determine timeline and offer structure-standard compliance issue but precedent-setting if Quest uses an unconventional exemption or if CESC board contests the valuation.
detail: Quest Capital Markets Limited has submitted a Regulation 31(4) disclosure to NSE under the SEBI (Substantial Acquisition of Shares and Takeovers) Regulations, 2011, in relation to CESC Limited (formerly Calcutta Electric Supply Company), a listed power distribution and generation utility headquartered in Mumbai. Regulation 31(4) requires disclosure of acquisition of shares in a target company when a person acquires shares bringing their holding to a notifiable threshold (typically 25% or higher, or triggering an open offer obligation). CESC is a material asset in India's power sector; any substantial change in control carries regulatory implications under the Electricity Act 2003 and the Tariff regulations. The filing does not yet disclose the precise percentage acquired, consideration, or timeline for a full open offer announcement, pending regulatory review.

framework.ref: SEBI (Substantial Acquisition of Shares and Takeovers) Regulations, 2011 - Regulation 31(4)
framework.note: Mandatory disclosure of acquisition crossing notifiable thresholds (25%, 51%, etc.); triggers open offer obligation unless exempted.
Exemptions from open offer (creeping acquisition, exempted persons, preferential allotment) - Quest may argue eligibility.

framework.ref: Securities and Exchange Board of India Act, 1992 - Section 15
framework.note: SEBI's authority to regulate takeovers and ensure fair disclosure.

framework.ref: Electricity Act, 2003 - Sections 39–41 (captive generation), Section 66 (power distribution regulation)
framework.note: Change of control in a distribution licensee (CESC) requires state regulator (MERC) approval; sector-specific regulatory gate.
If Quest's acquisition crosses CCI thresholds (asset value ₹2,500 cr or revenue ₹7,500 cr), prior CCI approval required under Section 6(1)(b).
If any party has unpaid dues to creditors, may trigger disqualification from resolution plan sponsorship (not typically relevant to open offer, but relevant if restructuring angle).

framework.ref: Foreign Exchange Management Act, 1999 - Regulation 8 (FDI in power distribution)
framework.note: If Quest or its sponsors are foreign entities, FDI approval from RBI/FIPB required for power sector investment.

framework.ref: Listing Regulations (SEBI LODR), 2015 - Regulation 30 (Related Party Transactions), Regulation 36 (Board approval)
framework.note: CESC board must approve related-party implications and disclosure timelines.

conditions: Crossing of notifiable threshold (threshold and percentage not yet disclosed in filing)
MERC/State regulator approval (for power distribution control change)
FDI clearance (if Quest or sponsors are foreign entities)
SEBI approval of open offer document (if exemption not granted)
approvals: SEBI Takeover Regulation 31(4) disclosure accepted by NSE
CCI approval (under Competition Act, 2002, Section 6 - if thresholds crossed)
Maharashtra Electricity Regulatory Commission (MERC) approval (Electricity Act, 2003)
RBI/FIPB FDI clearance (if cross-border or foreign sponsor involvement)
structure.novel: No publicly disclosed novel structuring; filing is routine Regulation 31(4) disclosure. Awaiting full open offer announcement for detail on consideration, timeline, and exemption claims (if any).

triggers.note: Substantial acquisition threshold (25%+) triggers mandatory open offer unless exempted under Regulation 37.
Combination (asset value ₹2,500 cr or revenue ₹7,500 cr) requires prior CCI approval; power utilities often trigger this threshold.
Control of a distribution licensee requires state regulator (MERC) approval; sector-specific gate affecting timing and terms.
If Quest or sponsor is foreign, FDI approval mandatory for power sector acquisition.
